refuted_approach: Affine GF(2) generators G: {0,1}^k -> {0,1}^n with k < n (seed-enumeration PRG candidates) fail the single parity test s.x. Proof: the image of an affine map has dimension at most k < n, so it lies in an affine hyperplane {x : s.x = b} for some s != 0, and the parity s.x is constant on the image. The parity is a THR o THR circuit with n bottom gates and top weights (+1,-1,+1,...) at threshold 1. So the error is |Pr_G[s.x=1] - Pr_U[s.x=1]| = 1/2. Scope: refutes the affine class only, not the lane.

lemma: Parity-bias lemma (candidate, does not close G0001). Let G: {0,1}^r -> {0,1}^n be any map and bias(s) = E_y[(-1)^(s.G(y))] for s in {0,1}^n. Then max over s != 0 of bias(s)^2 is at least (2^(n-r) - 1)/(2^n - 1), hence at least about 2^(-r). Proof: by Fourier inversion, sum over all s of bias(s)^2 = 2^n * Pr_{y,y'}[G(y) = G(y')]. By Cauchy-Schwarz over the image, the collision probability is at least 1/|Im G| >= 2^(-r). The s = 0 term is 1, so the sum over s != 0 is at least 2^(n-r) - 1. Averaging over the 2^n - 1 nonzero s gives the bound.

lemma: Exact parity-error formula for degree-2 generators. Let G(y) = (y, Z(y)) for y in GF(2)^k, Z_i(y) = l_i(y) + q_i(y), where q_i is a sum of monomials y_a y_b with a != b, and let B_e = sum_i e_i B_i over GF(2) for e in GF(2)^c, where B_i is the zero-diagonal symmetric matrix of q_i. Let h_e = rank(B_e)/2. Then max over nonzero tests s in GF(2)^n of |Pr_y[s.G(y)=1] - 1/2| = max over nonzero e of 2^(-1-h_e). PROOF: a test s=(a,e) gives s.G(y) = (a + sum_i e_i l_i).y + q_e(y), with q_e = sum_i e_i q_i. Choosing a to cancel the linear part (a is free) gives |bias| = |E_y (-1)^{q_e(y)}|. For a quadratic form over GF(2)^k whose alternating form has rank 2h, the sum of (-1)^q is 0 or +-2^(k-h) (radical argument), so |bias| = 2^(-h), and the error is |bias|/2. Other choices of a give 0 or the same magnitude, so the maximum is 2^(-h_e-1). For e=0 the test is the linear form a.y, error 0.

lemma: Corank tail and union bound for random degree-2 parity-fooling generators. (i) Let B be uniform over k x k alternating GF(2) matrices and d >= 1. Then P[corank B >= d] <= 4 * 2^(-d(d-1)/2). Proof: fix a d-dimensional subspace W. The map B -> P^T B P is a bijection on alternating matrices, so we may take W = span(e_1..e_d). Then W is contained in ker B iff the C(k,2) - C(k-d,2) = dk - d(d+1)/2 upper-triangular entries touching the first d coordinates vanish, so P[W in ker B] = 2^(-(dk - d(d+1)/2)). The number of d-dim subspaces is the Gaussian binomial [k choose d]_2 <= 4 * 2^(d(k-d)). A union bound over W gives P[corank >= d] <= 4 * 2^(d(k-d) - dk + d(d+1)/2) = 4 * 2^(-d(d-1)/2). (ii) Let k = n - c and G(y) = (y, Z(y)) for y in GF(2)^k, with Z_i(y) = l_i(y) + q_i(y), where q_i has alternating matrix B_i and l_i is linear; all B_i and l_i independent and uniform. For nonzero e in GF(2)^c, B_e = sum_i e_i B_i is uniform alternating. Union bound over the 2^c - 1 vectors e: P[some nonzero e has corank(B_e) >= d] <= 4 * 2^(c - d(d-1)/2). With d = ceil(sqrt(2c)) + 2 we get d(d-1)/2 >= c + sqrt(2c), so this probability is <= 4 * 2^(-sqrt(2c)). (iii) On the complementary event, the parity-error formula (earlier lemma) gives, for every nonzero parity test s = (a, e), |Pr[s.G(y) = 1] - 1/2| <= 2^(-1-h_e) with h_e = rank(B_e)/2 >= (k-d+1)/2, so the error is at most 2^(-(k-d+3)/2). Consequence: for c -> infinity with d = O(sqrt c) = o(n), a seed-length-(n-c) map G fools all parity tests of its outputs with error 2^(-Omega(n)), and the failure probability over the random choice is at most 4 * 2^(-sqrt(2c)) -> 0.

lemma: EXPLICIT ALTERNATING RANK-METRIC FAMILY (m odd). F = GF(2^m), Tr = absolute trace, B_alpha(x,y) = Tr(alpha(x*y^2 + x^2*y)) for alpha in F. (a) Each B_alpha is an alternating bilinear form over GF(2): B_alpha(x,x) = Tr(alpha(x^3+x^3)) = 0. (b) alpha -> B_alpha is GF(2)-linear. (c) For alpha != 0, rad(B_alpha) = {0, x_alpha} where x_alpha^3 = 1/alpha, hence rank(B_alpha) = m-1. Proof of (c): since Tr(z)=Tr(z^2), Tr(alpha x y^2) = Tr((alpha x)^{1/2} y), so B_alpha(x,.) = 0 iff (alpha x)^{1/2} + alpha x^2 = 0. Squaring (injective) gives alpha x + alpha^2 x^4 = 0, i.e. x = 0 or alpha x^3 = 1. For m odd gcd(3, 2^m-1) = 1, so x -> x^3 is a bijection on F*, giving exactly one nonzero root. Consequence (parity only): for k = m, c = m, n = 2k, define G(y) = (y, Z(y)), y in GF(2)^k, Z_i quadratic with polar matrix B_{2^(i-1)} (any linear part). For every nonzero parity test s = (a,e), s.G is quadratic plus affine with polar form B_e of rank k-1, so by the quadratic-form Gauss-sum bound |Pr[s.G(y)=1] - 1/2| <= 2^(-(k-1)/2).

lemma: EXTENDED ALTERNATING FAMILY (k >= 2, 1 <= c <= k). F = GF(2^k) with polynomial basis e_j = X^j, Tr = absolute trace, B_alpha(x,y) = Tr(alpha(x y^2 + x^2 y)). Let alpha_i = X^(i-1) for i = 1..c; these are GF(2)-linearly independent. Identify GF(2)^k with F via y -> sum_j y_j e_j, and set Z_i(y) = sum_{j<l} B_{alpha_i}(e_j, e_l) y_j y_l. Define G(y) = (y, Z_1(y), ..., Z_c(y)) in GF(2)^(k+c), so the seed is r = k. CLAIM: for every nonzero test s = (a, e) in GF(2)^(k+c), |Pr_y[s.G(y) = 1] - 1/2| <= 2^(-(k+1)/2). PROOF: If e = 0 then s.G = a.y is linear with a != 0, so the bias is 0. If e != 0, alpha_e = sum_i e_i alpha_i != 0 by independence. By the (c) part of the previous lemma (k odd), B_{alpha_e} has radical of dimension exactly 1. Q_e(y) = sum_i e_i Z_i(y) is quadratic with polar form B_{alpha_e}, so s.G(y) = Q_e(y) + a.y. The standard quadratic-form Gauss sum bound states that for a quadratic Q over GF(2)^k with polar radical of dimension d, sum_y (-1)^(Q(y) + linear) is 0 or of absolute value 2^((k+d)/2). With d = 1 the expectation E[(-1)^(s.G)] has absolute value at most 2^(-(k-1)/2). Since Pr[f=1] - 1/2 = -E[(-1)^f]/2, the claim follows. QED (parity tests only).

lemma: RADICAL LEMMA (general, odd k). Let k be odd, F = GF(2^k), Tr the absolute trace, alpha in F^*, and B_alpha(x,y) = Tr(alpha(x y^2 + x^2 y)). Then the radical {x : B_alpha(x,y) = 0 for all y} has exactly 2 elements. PROOF: Put h = 2^(k-1). Since Tr(z^2) = Tr(z), Tr(alpha x y^2) = Tr((alpha x y^2)^h) = Tr(alpha^h x^h y), using y^(2^k) = y. So B_alpha(x,y) = Tr(y L(x)) with L(x) = alpha^h x^h + alpha x^2, which is GF(2)-linear in x. The trace form is nondegenerate, so the radical equals ker L. Since (x^h)^2 = x^(2^k) = x, we have x^h = sqrt(x). For x in F: L(x) = 0 iff alpha x^2 = alpha^h sqrt(x). Squaring is a bijection of F, so this is equivalent to alpha^2 x^4 = alpha^(2h) x, i.e. x = 0 or x^3 = c with c = alpha^(2h-2) != 0. Since 2^k = 2 mod 3 for k odd, gcd(3, 2^k - 1) = 1, so cubing is a bijection of F^*, and x^3 = c has exactly one solution in F^*. Hence ker L = {0, x_0}. QED.

Setting: k odd >= 3, F = GF(2^k), n = 2k, seed r = k, G(y) = (y, Tr(beta_1 y^3), ..., Tr(beta_k y^3)) with beta_i = X^(i-1), y uniform on F. PROOF: write F(z) = sum_S Fhat(S) chi_S(z), chi_S(z) = (-1)^(sum_{i in S} z_i). Then E_y F(G(y)) - E_x F(x) = sum_{S != empty} Fhat(S) E_y (-1)^(<S, G(y)>), since E_x chi_S(x) = 0 for S != empty. For S != empty, z -> <S,z> is a nonzero GF(2)-linear functional, so by S0020 (applied with c = k) the bias b_S = Pr_y[<S,G(y)> = 0] - 1/2 satisfies |b_S| <= 2^(-(k+1)/2), hence |E_y (-1)^(<S,G(y)>)| = 2|b_S| <= 2^(-(k-1)/2). Therefore |E_y F(G(y)) - E_x F(x)| <= 2^(-(k-1)/2) L(f). Since Pr[f = 1] = (1 - E F)/2, the claim follows. QED. COROLLARY (conditional): for any threshold gate h_{w,t}(x) = [w.x >= t] on n bits, the error is <= 2^(-(k+1)/2) * L(h). Using the (unproved here, to be source-checked) bound sup_{w,t} L(THR_n) <= poly(n), the error is 2^(-n/4) poly(n) = o(1) with seed n/2 <= n - omega(log n). It does NOT cover XOR2 o THR o THR: L(f) of a depth-2 composition is not polynomially bounded by this method (the bound 2^(n/2) from Cauchy-Schwarz is trivial here, since 2^(-(k+1)/2) * 2^(n/2) >= 1).

Hand review of the parity-fooling lemma (odd k, G_c(y) = (y, Tr(beta_i y^3))_{i<=c}, c <= k, beta_i = X^(i-1)). (1) Linear independence: beta_1..beta_c are polynomial-basis elements, so gamma = sum e_i beta_i = 0 iff e = 0; then T(G_c(y)) = Tr(lambda y) with lambda != 0 gives bias 0. (2) Polar form: q(y)=Tr(gamma y^3 + lambda y) satisfies q(x+y)+q(x)+q(y) = B(x,y) = Tr(gamma(x^2 y + x y^2)). (3) Radical: z in R iff Tr(gamma(x^2 z + x z^2)) = 0 for all x iff (gamma z)^(1/2) + gamma z^2 = 0 iff gamma z (1 + gamma z^3) = 0, so R = {0} union {z : z^3 = 1/gamma}.
